correctness.rationale: For all \(p\ge5\) the forty-eight explicit line equations determine a connected 14-regular graph with 336 edges. Direct rank tests against three prime-field realization matrices match all congruence adjacencies. Frobenius permutes odd exponents modulo eight, so its effect on degree-zero divisors is the explicitly constructed integral \(P_q\). The graph Jacobian coinvariants have presentation \([R\mid P_q-I]\); the canonical perfect monodromy pairing makes their group dual to the fixed subgroup. Independent published full-group exponent 5760 and order \(2^{115}3^{28}5^6\) bound the prime support and valuations. The executable exact modular unimodular Smith algorithm resolves all local factors at moduli \(2^9,3^5,5^3\), reassembles groups and repeats every case with three distinct reduced-Laplacian roots. No inference from finite samples to the uniform characteristic claim is made; the root-of-unity line proof supplies it. The package verifier ran to the declared success marker.

value.rationale: The graph is canonically defined by the complete set of geometric lines on the Fermat quartic. Its fixed integral Jacobian is a mathematically natural refinement of the known ordinary graph group and arithmetic divisor rank. The complete q-mod8 classification distinguishes retention of all 5-primary torsion at \(q\equiv5\) from survival of only \(5^3\) at \(q\equiv3,7\), while two distinct nontrivial Frobenius actions happen to have identical invariant groups. This is a precise, nontrivial arithmetic invariant of a classical K3 curve configuration, not a normalization or parameter re-labelling.
